Subject: StitchBox P95 latency surge — coordination, mitigations, and customer note

Team —

We observed a sharp P95 jump on StitchBox's gen endpoints starting ~08:50 PDT (spike sustained across ~40 minutes). Metrics summary attached (p95-spike-traces.zip) — two buckets: short requests (<=128 tokens) and long requests (>512 tokens) both moved. Initial telemetry suggests increased RT for KV lookups (higher KV LRU churn) plus a small uptick in kernel queueing on a subset of instances serving their tenant pool.

Immediate asks:
- Ben / SRE: can you confirm whether this is caused by KV cache evaporation or scheduling contention? A quick flamegraph and per-host cache-hit heatmap would help.
- Marcus / Infra: can we push protective routing (route StitchBox to stable variant) for next 2 hrs if needed?
- Marissa / Product: I'll need a short customer-facing note (1–2 paragraphs) to send to Alice at StitchBox. If we implement protective routing or an expedited rollback of the quantization pilot, include impact and ETA.

Attached: p95-spike-traces.zip (trace snippets, host list), rollout-timeline.csv

I will coordinate exec escalation only if we need SLA credits; hold off until we confirm root cause.

-Kim
Senior Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: StitchBox P95 latency surge — coordination, mitigations, and customer note

Kim —

Quick update after 20m triage:
- Root candidate: KV cache churn on the host pool pinned to StitchBox. Hit-rate dropped ~22% on several hosts that had high eviction rates (confirmed by memstats).
- Secondary: we see burst kernel-queue length spikes on 3 accelerated instances (nvlink interop) coincident with the largest requests. Not CPU saturation, more serialization at the runtimes's attention kernel.

Short term mitigations we can enact in parallel (low risk):
1) Protective routing: move StitchBox traffic to their coldpool (older stable instances) for ~1–3 hours. This adds ~40ms median but reduces P95 by estimated 30–45%.
2) Disable the quantization pilot for StitchBox (pilot applies to small fraction of models) — this is a fast config flip and will restore prior kernel path.
3) Increase KV cache capacity for their pool (requires node resize — ~30m lead).

I recommend 2) then 1) if P95 doesn't come down in 10m. I'm attaching the flamegraphs in the zip (see p95-spike-traces.zip). Marcus: can you prepare the routing change and the config toggle? Marissa / Neha: please review the customer messaging below; I'll add a short technical blurb if we send the note.

-ben
SRE

Hi Alice —

Wanted to let you know we observed an elevated P95 on your Generation API starting at ~08:50 PDT this morning. Our SRE team investigated and identified increased KV cache evictions combined with transient runtime queueing on a subset of instances handling your pool.

What we did: disabled a small quantization pilot for your model, and (if needed) we will route traffic to a stable instance pool to mitigate tail latency. These actions are expected to restore typical P95 within 30–60 minutes.

What this means for you: you may see a small median latency increase (~30–40ms) if we route to cold pool; otherwise quality/outputs are unchanged. We do not expect data loss.

Next steps: we will follow up with a short post-incident note including root cause and long-term mitigations (KV sizing and conservative warmup for pilot rollouts).

Apologies for the interruption — we understand the impact and are prioritizing stability.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Incident: Elevated P95 latency on Generation API (Aug 3)

Alice —

We wanted to update you directly: earlier today we detected an elevated P95 on StitchBox's Generation API (began ~08:50 PDT). Our SRE team investigated and found increased KV cache evictions on hosts pinned to your tenant plus transient runtime queueing on a small set of accelerated instances.

Actions taken so far:
- We disabled a targeted quantization pilot for your model (completed at 09:45 PDT).
- SRE prepared a protective routing plan; we did not need to activate it after the config flip, as P95 recovered to expected levels within ~45 minutes.

Impact: you may have seen delayed responses during the spike window. We do not believe any requests were dropped and there is no data loss. If you noticed anything that looks like degraded output quality, please forward examples to us and we'll prioritize.

Next steps: we're scheduling a post-incident review with infra/serving to harden pilot rollouts and add on-host warmup and stricter KV sizing for tenant pools. Will share the RCA and timeline within 48 hours.

Appreciate your patience — we know this impacts your users.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Ops | Redwood Inference
